_comment: Editorial decoration for the TSDynamics system catalogue. The registry (registry.all_systems()) is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for every fact: name, family, category, dim, params, variables, reference, doi, known_lyapunov, _field_shape. This file ONLY decorates: human display names for subcategories/types, prose blurbs, parameter role notes, plot-dt overrides, projection picks for 4D+ systems, and behavior tags. NEVER put computed quantities (Lyapunov spectra, fractal dimensions, Kaplan-Yorke) here — those are computed at build time. Editorial keys that do not match a registry system are ignored harmlessly; registry systems with no editorial entry render without decoration. Seeded from design/brand/data/systems.json and reconciled against the live registry.

type_blurbs.ode: Continuous-time systems. Write the right-hand side; TSDynamics lowers it to the Rust engine and integrates with adaptive Dormand–Prince, implicit BDF, or fixed-step schemes.
type_blurbs.dde: Feedback with a finite memory. Supply the delays and a history function; TSDynamics integrates by the method of steps with dense interpolation of the past.
type_blurbs.sde: Systems driven by noise. Provide drift and diffusion; TSDynamics integrates with Euler–Maruyama or Milstein and returns ensembles, moments, and the deterministic skeleton.
type_blurbs.map: Discrete-time systems. Iterate orbits, cobweb and bifurcation diagrams, and Lyapunov exponents directly — no integration needed.

subcategory_blurbs.chaotic_attractors: Dissipative flows with a positive Lyapunov exponent that settle onto a strange attractor — bounded, aperiodic, sensitive to initial conditions.
subcategory_blurbs.chem_bio_systems: Reaction kinetics and excitable cells. Mass-action and Hill-type nonlinearities give oscillations, bistability, and spikes.
subcategory_blurbs.climate_geophysics: Low-order truncations of atmosphere, ocean, and flow — capturing regime behavior, tipping, and reversals with a handful of modes.
subcategory_blurbs.coupled_systems: Engineered and coupled chaotic flows — generalized Lorenz/Chen-family attractors and interacting units.
subcategory_blurbs.exotic_systems: Minimal or unusual constructions — hyperchaotic, conservative, and engineered attractors of higher dimension.
subcategory_blurbs.oscillatory_systems: Organized around a limit cycle — self-sustained oscillation, relaxation cycles, tori, and forced resonance.
subcategory_blurbs.physical_systems: Mechanical and electrical models from first principles — pendula, circuits, lasers, and few-body motion.
subcategory_blurbs.population_dynamics: Interacting species and resources — cycles, coexistence, and predator–prey coevolution.
subcategory_blurbs.spatial_fields: Spatially extended PDEs reduced to large ODE systems by method-of-lines — pattern formation and spatiotemporal chaos.
subcategory_blurbs.delayed_systems: The rate depends on the state τ ago — a scalar variable becomes effectively infinite-dimensional, giving high-dimensional chaos from one line.
subcategory_blurbs.stochastic_systems: Deterministic skeletons perturbed by Wiener noise — mean reversion, escape, switching, and noise-induced transitions.
subcategory_blurbs.chaotic_maps: Aperiodic, exponentially sensitive orbits — the simplest route to chaos.
subcategory_blurbs.exotic_maps: Strange and ornamental attractors — iterated trigonometric and polynomial maps prized for their structure.
subcategory_blurbs.geometric_maps: Area-preserving and piecewise-linear maps — mixing, horseshoes, circle and toral dynamics.
subcategory_blurbs.polynomial_maps: Low-degree polynomial maps — the canonical setting for period-doubling and renormalization.
subcategory_blurbs.population_maps: Discrete-generation ecology — single-species recruitment and host–parasitoid models.

Lorenz.blurb: The 1963 convection model — three coupled quadratic ODEs whose butterfly attractor launched modern chaos theory.

Rossler.blurb: A single-folded-band attractor built from the minimal nonlinearity — one quadratic term — yet fully chaotic.

Chen.blurb: A dual to Lorenz with the opposite sign convention — a generalized chaotic flow in the Lorenz family.

param_roles.a: coupling gain of the x-y channel
param_roles.b: linear decay rate of the z channel
param_roles.c: self-feedback gain of the y channel

Chua.blurb: The double-scroll attractor of Chua's circuit — the canonical electronic chaos generator.

param_roles.m0: inner slope of the piecewise-linear Chua diode
param_roles.m1: outer slope of the piecewise-linear Chua diode

Thomas.blurb: Cyclically symmetric flow whose 27 equilibria and labyrinthine trajectories arise from pure sinusoidal feedback.

Halvorsen.blurb: A cyclically symmetric quadratic flow with a tightly wound multi-scroll attractor.

param_roles.b: coupling coefficient between the three variables

Aizawa.blurb: An ornamental forced attractor with a pinched-torus geometry — the TSDynamics signature shape.

Dadras.blurb: A multi-wing chaotic flow with adjustable scroll count.

NoseHoover.blurb: A conservative thermostatted oscillator — chaos without dissipation, sampling a canonical ensemble.

RabinovichFabrikant.blurb: A flow from plasma physics with stiff, spiky excursions and a delicate attractor.

RikitakeDynamo.blurb: A two-disk dynamo whose chaotic reversals model the geomagnetic field flipping polarity.

param_roles.a: asymmetry / coupling between the two disks

Lorenz84.blurb: Lorenz's low-order atmospheric circulation model — regime behavior in the mid-latitude jet.

Lorenz96.blurb: A ring of advectively coupled sites — the standard testbed for atmospheric data assimilation and spatiotemporal chaos.

Rucklidge.blurb: A model of convection in an imposed magnetic field — a compact chaotic flow.

BurkeShaw.blurb: A symmetric chaotic flow derived from the Lorenz template.

param_roles.e: constant forcing on the z channel
param_roles.n: common coupling / timescale scaling the cross terms

KuramotoSivashinsky.blurb: The canonical 1-D model of spatiotemporal chaos — flame fronts and falling films, chaotic in space and time.

param_roles.L: domain length (sets the number of unstable modes)

GrayScott.blurb: A reaction–diffusion system whose spots, stripes, and self-replicating patterns are a landmark of Turing morphogenesis.

param_roles.N: grid points per side (structural — changing it recompiles)

SwiftHohenberg.blurb: The prototype pattern-forming PDE — stripes and hexagons from a single scalar field near a finite-wavelength instability.

param_roles.N: grid points per side (structural — changing it recompiles)

VanDerPol.blurb: The archetypal relaxation oscillator — nonlinear damping pumps small swings and bleeds large ones, so every orbit lands on one and the same limit cycle.

param_roles.mu: nonlinear damping strength (0 = harmonic, >> 1 = relaxation oscillator)

ForcedVanDerPol.blurb: Van der Pol under periodic forcing — frequency entrainment and the route to chaos.

Duffing.blurb: A driven double-well oscillator — the textbook forced-chaos system with a fractal basin boundary.

param_roles.omega: angular frequency of the periodic forcing

MooreSpiegel.blurb: A thermo-mechanical oscillator from stellar convection — aperiodic pulsation.

StuartLandau.blurb: The normal form of a supercritical Hopf bifurcation — an exactly circular limit cycle of radius √mu, the reference case for every limit-cycle method.

param_roles.b: nonlinear frequency shift (shear); b = 0 is isochronous
param_roles.mu: distance past the Hopf bifurcation (cycle radius √mu)
param_roles.omega: linear angular frequency at the bifurcation

ShimizuMorioka.blurb: A symmetric reduction of Lorenz-like dynamics near a homoclinic bifurcation.

Torus.blurb: Quasiperiodic motion on a 2-torus — two incommensurate frequencies, no chaos.

Lissajous2D.blurb: A planar Lissajous figure — the elementary two-frequency oscillation.

param_roles.delta: phase shift of y relative to x

Lissajous3D.blurb: A three-frequency Lissajous curve traced on a torus.

param_roles.delta_y: phase shift of y relative to x
param_roles.delta_z: phase shift of z relative to x

DoublePendulum.blurb: Two coupled pendula — the iconic mechanically chaotic system, exquisitely sensitive to initial conditions.

param_roles.d: arm length (sets the gravitational frequency scale)

HenonHeiles.blurb: A galactic potential whose bounded motion transitions from regular tori to chaos with energy.

param_roles.lam: strength of the cubic anharmonic coupling

Colpitts.blurb: The Colpitts LC oscillator driven into chaos — a real electronic circuit model.

param_roles.a: loop-gain / nonlinearity strength of the transistor term
param_roles.b: damping (loss) coefficient on the voltage y

Laser.blurb: A single-mode laser (Haken) — the Lorenz equations in optical disguise.

param_roles.a: linear coupling / decay rate between x and y
param_roles.b: strength of the cubic y*z^2 coupling driving x
param_roles.k: strength of the quadratic x^2 feedback into z

JerkCircuit.blurb: A minimal third-order 'jerk' circuit — chaos from one nonlinear element.

SwingingAtwood.blurb: The swinging Atwood machine — a mass on a pulley that swings into chaotic motion.

param_roles.m2: non-swinging counterweight mass (ratio m2/m1 controls the dynamics)

WindmiReduced.blurb: A reduced model of the magnetosphere–ionosphere coupling (WINDMI) — substorm dynamics.

param_roles.a1: linear coupling coefficient of the reduced model
param_roles.b1: linear coupling coefficient of the reduced model
param_roles.b2: linear coupling coefficient of the reduced model
param_roles.b3: linear coupling coefficient of the reduced model
param_roles.d1: steepness of the tanh substorm-onset switch

HindmarshRose.blurb: A three-variable neuron model reproducing spiking and bursting with chaotic interspike patterns.

param_roles.a: coefficient of the cubic spike term
param_roles.b: coefficient of the quadratic spike term
param_roles.c: constant of the fast recovery dynamics
param_roles.d: constant of the fast recovery dynamics
param_roles.s: strength of the slow adaptation feedback
param_roles.tx: timescale constant of the fast (x) variable
param_roles.tz: timescale constant of the slow (z) variable

FitzHughNagumo.blurb: The two-variable nerve membrane — a fast cubic voltage coupled to a slow recovery current: excitable at rest, spiking under an applied current.

param_roles.a: offset of the linear recovery nullcline
param_roles.b: slope of the linear recovery nullcline

ForcedFitzHughNagumo.blurb: The forced FitzHugh–Nagumo excitable cell — periodic stimulation of a spiking neuron.

param_roles.a: constant of the slow recovery dynamics
param_roles.b: constant of the slow recovery dynamics
param_roles.omega: angular frequency of the periodic stimulus

Oregonator.blurb: The Field–Körös–Noyes model of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction — chemical relaxation oscillations.

param_roles.q: scaled rate-constant ratio of the bromide-consuming steps
param_roles.f: stoichiometric factor for catalyst regeneration (bifurcation parameter)

Selkov.blurb: The minimal glycolytic clock — one product-activation loop, and a limit cycle for every substrate supply inside the Hopf window.

param_roles.a: scaled reverse rate of the enzyme (oscillations need a < 1/8)
param_roles.b: scaled substrate supply rate — the bifurcation parameter

GlycolyticOscillation.blurb: Decroly and Goldbeter's multiply-regulated glycolytic oscillator — two product-activated enzymes in series, giving birhythmicity and chaos (the three-variable extension of the planar Selkov model).

param_roles.d: cooperativity modulation of the second enzyme
param_roles.k: removal (sink) rate of the final product
param_roles.l1: allosteric constant of the first enzyme
param_roles.l2: allosteric constant of the second enzyme
param_roles.nu: constant input rate of the substrate
param_roles.q1: coupling ratio linking the two enzymatic stages
param_roles.q2: coupling ratio linking the two enzymatic stages
param_roles.s1: maximum rate of the first allosteric enzyme
param_roles.s2: maximum rate of the second allosteric enzyme

Brusselator.blurb: Prigogine and Lefever's autocatalytic reaction — the textbook dissipative structure, oscillating for b above the Hopf threshold 1 + a².

param_roles.a: constant feed of the activator x
param_roles.b: feed driving the autocatalytic loop (Hopf at b = 1 + a²)

ForcedBrusselator.blurb: The Brusselator under periodic forcing — entrainment and chaos in an autocatalytic reaction.

param_roles.a: constant feed of the activator x

HastingsPowell.blurb: A three-trophic food chain whose tea-cup attractor is a landmark of ecological chaos.

param_roles.a1: maximum attack rate of the consumer on the resource
param_roles.a2: maximum attack rate of the predator on the consumer
param_roles.d2: death rate of the top predator

CellCycle.blurb: A model of the eukaryotic cell-division oscillator.

param_roles.K: common Michaelis constant of the modification cycles
param_roles.Kc: threshold for cdk activation by cyclin
param_roles.Kim: inhibition constant of the mutual coupling

CircadianRhythm.blurb: A molecular circadian clock — entrainable biochemical oscillation.

param_roles.Ki: threshold for repression by nuclear PER
param_roles.k: phosphorylation / turnover rate of cytosolic PER
param_roles.k1: transport rate of PER into the nucleus
param_roles.k2: transport rate of PER out of the nucleus
param_roles.kd: Michaelis constant of cytosolic PER degradation
param_roles.kdn: Michaelis constant of nuclear PER degradation
param_roles.ks: rate of PER synthesis from mRNA
param_roles.vd: maximum degradation rate of cytosolic PER
param_roles.vdn: maximum degradation rate of nuclear PER
param_roles.vmax: upper bound of the phase-modulated transcription rate
param_roles.vmin: lower bound of the phase-modulated transcription rate

MackeyGlass.blurb: A single delayed feedback loop modeling blood-cell production — the canonical high-dimensional delay chaos.

param_roles.tau: feedback delay (raise it to climb the period-doubling cascade into chaos)

IkedaDelay.blurb: A delayed optical-cavity model — sinusoidal nonlinearity with memory, chaotic for modest delay.

param_roles.c: linear relaxation (damping) rate of the cavity field
param_roles.x0: phase offset (detuning) of the nonlinear feedback

SprottDelay.blurb: A minimal scalar delay equation engineered for chaos from one nonlinear term.

ScrollDelay.blurb: A delayed feedback circuit producing multi-scroll attractors in the embedding.

param_roles.alpha: linear decay rate of the delayed state
param_roles.beta: gain of the saturating tanh feedback

PiecewiseCircuit.blurb: A delayed piecewise-linear circuit — chaos from a saturating nonlinearity with memory.

param_roles.alpha: linear decay rate of the delayed state
param_roles.beta: gain of the cubic feedback term
param_roles.c: scale of the cubic nonlinearity (feedback hump width)

OrnsteinUhlenbeck.blurb: The canonical mean-reverting process — linear restoring drift plus additive noise, the Gaussian stationary benchmark.

GeometricBrownianMotion.blurb: Multiplicative noise — the log-normal process underlying Black–Scholes and population growth under uncertainty.

DoubleWell.blurb: A particle in a bistable potential driven by noise — noise-induced switching between the two wells.

param_roles.a: curvature of the potential at the origin (barrier / well locations)

Logistic.blurb: The logistic map — one quadratic line whose period-doubling cascade is the textbook road to chaos.

Henon.blurb: The Hénon map — a 2-D quadratic map whose folded attractor is the canonical strange attractor of dissipative maps.

Tent.blurb: The piecewise-linear tent map — exact, fully chaotic, conjugate to the binary shift.

Chirikov.blurb: The Chirikov standard map — the paradigm of Hamiltonian chaos, mixing tori and chaotic seas.

param_roles.K: kick strength (controls the transition to global chaos)

Ikeda.blurb: The Ikeda map — a spiral strange attractor from a nonlinear optical ring cavity.

param_roles.a: phase-offset constant of the cavity detuning

Tinkerbell.blurb: An ornamental 2-D quadratic map whose attractor resembles a fairy in flight.

Gingerbreadman.blurb: A piecewise-linear map tiling the plane with quasiperiodic gingerbread-man cells.

Ulam.blurb: The Ulam map (logistic at r=4) — exactly chaotic with a known invariant density.

param_roles.a: map offset (a=1 gives the ergodic regime)
param_roles.b: quadratic gain (b=2 gives the ergodic regime)

Baker.blurb: The baker's map — stretch, cut, and stack; the cleanest model of mixing and the horseshoe.

param_roles.alpha: fold fraction splitting the height (0.5 = area-preserving)

Circle.blurb: The circle map — mode-locking, Arnold tongues, and the devil's staircase.

Chebyshev.blurb: Iterated Chebyshev polynomials — exactly chaotic maps of the interval.

param_roles.a: map degree (integer a>=2 gives Lyapunov exponent ln a)

Gauss.blurb: The Gauss (continued-fraction) map — number-theoretic chaos on the unit interval.

param_roles.a: width of the Gaussian (larger a = narrower peak)
param_roles.b: vertical shift controlling the bifurcation cascade

Ricker.blurb: The Ricker recruitment map — over-compensatory density dependence driving fishery population cycles and chaos.

MaynardSmith.blurb: A 2-D ecological recruitment map with delayed density dependence.

param_roles.a: damping / linear feedback on the current state

DeJong.blurb: A Peter de Jong attractor — a sinusoidal iterated map prized for its lacework structure.

KaplanYorke.blurb: The Kaplan–Yorke map — a skew product whose fractal dimension is known in closed form.

param_roles.alpha: contraction rate of the y coordinate (0<alpha<1)

param_roles.a: phase coefficient in the cos(a*x - y) term
param_roles.b: scale dividing the x*y product and the sin(y) term

GumowskiMira.blurb: The Gumowski–Mira map — accelerator-physics origin, endlessly varied ornamental phase portraits.  At the shipped defaults it is area-preserving: a chaotic sea threaded with periodic islands rather than an attractor.

param_roles.a: shape coefficient of the rational nonlinearity G
param_roles.b: linear feedback gain mixing the previous y

SprottA.blurb: Case A of Sprott's 1994 minimal-chaos search — a five-term conservative flow identical to the Nosé–Hoover thermostat, its chaotic sea threaded with invariant tori.

SprottB.blurb: Case B of Sprott's 1994 search for the algebraically simplest chaotic flows — five terms and two quadratic nonlinearities.

SprottC.blurb: Case C of Sprott's 1994 search for the algebraically simplest chaotic flows — five terms and two quadratic nonlinearities.

SprottD.blurb: Case D of Sprott's 1994 search for the algebraically simplest chaotic flows — five terms and two quadratic nonlinearities.

SprottE.blurb: Case E of Sprott's 1994 search for the algebraically simplest chaotic flows — five terms and two quadratic nonlinearities.

SprottF.blurb: Case F of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottG.blurb: Case G of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottH.blurb: Case H of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottK.blurb: Case K of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottL.blurb: Case L of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottM.blurb: Case M of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottN.blurb: Case N of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottO.blurb: Case O of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottP.blurb: Case P of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottQ.blurb: Case Q of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottR.blurb: Case R of Sprott's 1994 search for minimal chaotic flows — six terms with a single quadratic nonlinearity.

SprottJerk.blurb: The provably algebraically-simplest dissipative chaotic flow — a single-quadratic jerk system whose Möbius-strip attractor emerges by period doubling near mu ≈ 2.017.

SprottMore.blurb: A minimal jerk flow built from non-polynomial elementary functions — sign-function Coulomb damping plus a Gaussian nonlinearity.

SprottTorus.blurb: A time-reversible equilibrium-free flow that is conservative on nested invariant tori for some initial conditions and hosts a hidden strange attractor with a twin repellor for others.

Arneodo.blurb: A third-order jerk system with a cubic nonlinearity whose spiral Shilnikov attractor arises from a homoclinic bifurcation.

GuckenheimerHolmes.blurb: A symmetric flow with a structurally stable heteroclinic cycle — the prototype of cycling chaos, slowing near each saddle in turn.

HyperLorenz.blurb: A four-dimensional Lorenz extension with a feedback state that lifts the flow into hyperchaos — two positive Lyapunov exponents.

HyperRossler.blurb: Rössler's original four-dimensional flow — the first system shown to be hyperchaotic, with two positive Lyapunov exponents from a single quadratic term.

HyperYan.blurb: A four-dimensional flow with multiple cross-product nonlinearities and a feedback variable producing hyperchaos.

HyperYangChen.blurb: A four-dimensional Chen-like flow with an added linear feedback variable that yields hyperchaotic dynamics.

LorenzBounded.blurb: The Lorenz attractor reformulated with polynomial corrections that confine it to a bounded region, recovering the standard flow as r grows.

param_roles.r: bounding radius (larger r recovers unbounded Lorenz)

LorenzCoupled.blurb: Two identical Lorenz subsystems diffusively coupled through their x-variables — the canonical testbed for chaos synchronization.

param_roles.kappa: diffusive coupling strength between the two subsystems

MultiChua.blurb: A ring of Chua circuits coupled through their x-variables — multi-scroll chaos and synchronization from linked double-scroll units.

param_roles.m0: inner slope of the Chua diode
param_roles.m1: outer slope of the Chua diode
param_roles.n_circuits: number of circuits in the ring (structural — changing it recompiles)

PehlivanWei.blurb: A parameter-free three-dimensional flow with two quadratic nonlinearities, notable for its simple algebraic form and equilibrium structure.

ArnoldWeb.blurb: A perturbed three-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian whose overlapping resonance lines form the Arnold web governing slow chaotic diffusion in nearly integrable systems.

param_roles.mu: perturbation strength coupling the three actions through the web

CellularNeuralNetwork.blurb: A three-cell continuous-time cellular neural network with piecewise-linear saturation — a hardware-realizable circuit chaos generator.

HyperBao.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow formed by adding a linear feedback controller to the Lü system, giving two positive Lyapunov exponents.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y (Lü) subsystem
param_roles.d: gain of the y·z term feeding the auxiliary state w
param_roles.e: feedback gain of x onto w

HyperCai.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow augmenting a Lorenz-like chaotic core with a fourth feedback state, yielding two positive Lyapunov exponents.

param_roles.a: linear coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: linear gain in the y equation
param_roles.c: linear gain in the y equation
param_roles.d: damping of the z mode (fed by y²)
param_roles.e: feedback gain of the auxiliary state w onto x

HyperJha.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic extension of the Lorenz system with a fourth state coupled back through an x·z term, giving two positive Lyapunov exponents.

param_roles.a: Lorenz coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: Lorenz-like gain in the y equation
param_roles.d: self-gain of the auxiliary feedback state w

HyperLu.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow from state-feedback control of the Lü system, with two positive Lyapunov exponents verified by an electronic-circuit realization.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y (Lü) subsystem
param_roles.d: self-gain of the auxiliary feedback state w

HyperPang.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow built by adding a linear controller to the Lü system, with two positive Lyapunov exponents and a studied Hopf bifurcation.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y (Lü) subsystem
param_roles.d: feedback gain of x and y onto the auxiliary state w

HyperQi.blurb: A 4-D smooth quadratic system with two large positive Lyapunov exponents — a much-studied benchmark for hyperchaos synchronization and secure communication.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: linear gain in the y equation
param_roles.e: cross-coupling gain between the z and w states
param_roles.f: cross-coupling gain between the z and w states

HyperWang.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow with a Lorenz-like core, a quadratic x² drive on the z mode, and a fourth feedback state — two positive Lyapunov exponents.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: linear gain in the y equation
param_roles.d: feedback gain of x onto the auxiliary state w
param_roles.e: strength of the x² nonlinearity driving z

HyperXu.blurb: A 4-D hyperchaotic flow from state-feedback control of a chaotic core, with two positive Lyapunov exponents and an analog-circuit realization.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: linear gain in the y equation
param_roles.d: gain of the y feedback in the w equation
param_roles.e: strength of the x·z nonlinearity driving y

LorenzStenflo.blurb: Stenflo's four-dimensional generalization of Lorenz for finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves in a rotating atmosphere — hyperchaotic for suitable parameters.

param_roles.a: Prandtl-like number coupling x and y (and damping w)
param_roles.b: geometric damping of the z mode
param_roles.c: Rayleigh-like forcing in the y equation
param_roles.d: rotation parameter coupling the auxiliary state w into x

NewtonLiepnik.blurb: Euler's rigid-body equations with a linear feedback torque, producing two coexisting strange attractors selected by the initial basin.

param_roles.a: linear damping coefficient on the x mode
param_roles.b: linear gain on the z mode (the feedback parameter)

NuclearQuadrupole.blurb: A two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian for collective quadrupole vibrations of the nuclear surface, with a mixed regular–chaotic phase space that grows chaotic with energy.

param_roles.b: strength of the cubic anharmonic coupling between the two modes
param_roles.d: strength of the quartic anharmonic terms

Qi.blurb: A 4-D flow in which every equation carries a triple cross-product term, giving a four-wing chaotic attractor far more complex than the quadratic Lorenz family.

param_roles.a: coupling rate of the x–y subsystem
param_roles.b: linear gain in the y equation

Robinson.blurb: A Duffing-like double-well x–y oscillator coupled to a slow z mode driven by x², producing a Lorenz-type chaotic attractor.

param_roles.a: linear damping of the oscillator velocity y
param_roles.b: coefficient of the x²·y nonlinear damping term
param_roles.c: damping of the slow z mode
param_roles.d: gain of the x² forcing on z
param_roles.v: coupling strength of the y·z feedback term

Bouali2.blurb: An extended Van der Pol oscillator with a chaos-inducing feedback loop, proposed by Bouali as an idealised macroeconomic business-cycle model with a stretched-loop strange attractor.

param_roles.a: self-excitation gain of the oscillator core
param_roles.y0: reference level of the x channel
param_roles.b: feedback gain of the z channel into x
param_roles.g: nonlinear damping of the y channel

ChenLee.blurb: The governing equations of a gyro with internal-torque feedback, derived from the rigid-body Euler equations, generating a symmetric two-scroll attractor.

param_roles.a: self-feedback gain of the x channel
param_roles.b: self-feedback gain of the y channel
param_roles.c: self-feedback gain of the z channel

DequanLi.blurb: A Lorenz-family quadratic flow whose extra x*z and x**2 terms break the two-scroll structure into a three-scroll attractor.

param_roles.d: x*z cross-product strength in the x equation
param_roles.k: forcing gain of the y channel
param_roles.f: self-feedback gain of the y channel
param_roles.c: self-feedback gain of the z channel
param_roles.eps: x**2 term strength in the z equation

LuChen.blurb: The Lü attractor — a quadratic flow sitting at the transition between the Lorenz and Chen systems yet belonging to neither.

param_roles.c: self-feedback gain of the y channel
param_roles.b: linear decay rate of the z channel

LuChenCheng.blurb: A unified one-parameter family that interpolates continuously between the Lorenz and Chen attractors, staying chaotic across the whole transition.

param_roles.a: self-feedback gain of the y channel (sets x-channel decay with b)
param_roles.b: self-feedback gain of the z channel (sets x-channel decay with a)
param_roles.c: constant forcing on the x channel

QiChen.blurb: A Lorenz/Chen-template flow whose extra y*z term gives multiple equilibria and a four-wing chaotic attractor.

param_roles.c: forcing gain of x into y
param_roles.b: linear decay rate of the z channel

Sakarya.blurb: A six-term Lorenz-family flow, realised as an electronic circuit, whose y*z and x*z nonlinearities produce a butterfly-like attractor.

param_roles.a: self-feedback gain on the x channel
param_roles.b: self-feedback gain on the y channel
param_roles.c: self-feedback gain on the z channel

SanUmSrisuchinwong.blurb: A single-parameter chaotic flow built from just a z*tanh(x) term, a quadratic x*y product, and an abs(y) term — convenient for analogue-circuit realisation.

param_roles.a: constant forcing on the z channel (the single tunable parameter)

WangSun.blurb: A Wang–Sun quadratic flow carrying one cross-product nonlinearity per equation (y*z, x*z, x*y), producing a chaotic attractor.

param_roles.a: self-feedback gain on the x channel
param_roles.d: self-feedback gain on the y channel
param_roles.e: self-feedback gain on the z channel
param_roles.q: y*z cross-product strength in the x equation
param_roles.f: x*y cross-product strength in the z equation

YuWang.blurb: A Yu–Wang flow whose z equation carries a quadratic-exponential exp(x*y) nonlinearity, yielding a compound mirror-merged attractor unlike the purely quadratic Lorenz family.

param_roles.b: forcing gain of x into y
param_roles.c: x*z cross-product strength in the y equation
param_roles.d: linear decay rate of the z channel

YuWang2.blurb: A variant of the Yu–Wang flow with the exponential replaced by a cosh(x*y) term, again producing a compound chaotic attractor.

param_roles.b: forcing gain of x into y
param_roles.c: x*z cross-product strength in the y equation
param_roles.d: linear decay rate of the z channel

ZhouChen.blurb: A Zhou–Chen quadratic flow carrying paired y*z nonlinearities alongside x*z and x*y terms, producing a chaotic attractor.

param_roles.a: self-feedback gain on the x channel
param_roles.c: self-feedback gain on the y channel
param_roles.e: self-feedback gain on the z channel
param_roles.d: y*z cross-product strength in the y equation

ArnoldBeltramiChildress.blurb: An exact steady Beltrami solution of Euler's equations whose streamlines are generically chaotic — the classic example of Lagrangian chaos and fast-dynamo theory.

param_roles.a: amplitude of the first Beltrami component
param_roles.b: amplitude of the second Beltrami component
param_roles.c: amplitude of the third Beltrami component

AtmosphericRegime.blurb: Two coupled oscillators with widely spaced frequencies whose timescale separation drives intermittent bursts between quasi-stationary weather regimes.

param_roles.mu1: linear growth/damping of the slow mode
param_roles.mu2: linear growth/damping of the fast oscillator
param_roles.omega: natural frequency of the fast oscillator

BlinkingRotlet.blurb: A passive tracer stirred by two off-centre rotlets that alternate on and off, folding and stretching material lines into chaotic Stokes-flow advection.

DoubleGyre.blurb: A kinematic pair of counter-rotating gyres with a periodically oscillating separatrix — the canonical benchmark for Lagrangian coherent structures and chaotic advection.

Hadley.blurb: The Lorenz-84 caricature of the mid-latitude westerly circulation — a zonal current coupled to superposed eddies that yields irregular, intransitive weather.

param_roles.a: damping rate of the zonal flow
param_roles.f: symmetric thermal forcing of the zonal flow
param_roles.g: asymmetric thermal forcing of the eddies

OscillatingFlow.blurb: A kinematic array of convection rolls with laterally oscillating boundaries whose time-dependent separatrices chaotically transport tracers between adjacent cells.

RayleighBenard.blurb: A three-mode Saltzman truncation of thermal convection heated from below — the convection family from which the Lorenz attractor descends.

SaltonSea.blurb: An eco-epidemiological fish–bird disease model whose period-doubling route to chaos was proposed to explain observed mass die-offs at the Salton Sea.

param_roles.m: maximum predation rate on infected fish
param_roles.mu: disease-induced death rate of infected fish

VallisElNino.blurb: A Lorenz-like conceptual model of the tropical Pacific ocean–atmosphere that makes El Niño's aperiodicity intrinsic, with no stochastic forcing needed.

CaTwoPlus.blurb: A calcium-induced calcium-release oscillator with self-modulated InsP₃ signalling that produces spikes, bursting, chaos, and birhythmicity.

param_roles.V0: constant Ca²⁺ influx into the cytosol
param_roles.Vm2: maximum Ca²⁺ pumping rate into the store
param_roles.K5: Michaelis constant of the kinase flux
param_roles.m: Hill coefficient of the CICR term
param_roles.n: Hill coefficient of the CICR term
param_roles.p: Hill coefficient of the InsP₃-degradation term
param_roles.kf: passive Ca²⁺ leak from the store

ExcitableCell.blurb: The Chay conductance model of a bursting pancreatic β-cell — fast spiking gated by a slow Ca²⁺ wave, with period doubling and chaos across the beating–bursting transition.

param_roles.vm: half-activation voltage of the gating rate
param_roles.vn: half-activation voltage of the gating rate
param_roles.rho: slow-timescale factor of the Ca²⁺ dynamics

IsothermalChemical.blurb: The Petrov–Scott–Showalter isothermal autocatalator — cubic autocatalysis feeding a slow species, the canonical route to mixed-mode oscillations and chaos in unforced chemistry.

param_roles.kappa: feedback coupling of the slow species
param_roles.sigma: timescale ratio of the fast autocatalyst
param_roles.delta: timescale ratio of the slow species

ItikBanksTumor.blurb: A Lotka–Volterra-type cancer model of competing tumour, healthy, and immune cell populations whose interactions produce a strange attractor.

param_roles.a12: competition of healthy cells on the tumour
param_roles.a13: competition of immune cells on the tumour
param_roles.a21: competition of the tumour on healthy cells
param_roles.a31: inactivation rate of immune cells by the tumour
param_roles.r2: growth rate of healthy host cells
param_roles.d3: death rate of effector immune cells

TurchinHanski.blurb: An empirically grounded vole–weasel predator–prey model under seasonal forcing that reproduces the latitudinal gradient from stable cycles to chaos.

AnishchenkoAstakhov.blurb: A radiophysical self-oscillator with inertial nonlinearity — the canonical model of spiral (saddle-focus) chaos reached by the Feigenbaum period-doubling route.

param_roles.eta: inertial-relaxation rate of the nonlinear element
param_roles.mu: excitation parameter (negative damping of the circuit)

StickSlipOscillator.blurb: A harmonically forced dry-friction oscillator whose Stribeck velocity switch produces alternating stick and slip phases that can turn chaotic.

param_roles.a: linear stiffness of the Duffing restoring force
param_roles.b: cubic stiffness of the Duffing restoring force
param_roles.alpha: linear velocity coefficient of the friction torque
param_roles.beta: cubic velocity coefficient of the friction torque
param_roles.eps: coupling weight of the friction/forcing term
param_roles.w: angular frequency of the harmonic drive

Blasius.blurb: A three-level food chain with Holling type-II responses whose chaotic "teacup" attractor is a landmark of ecological chaos.

param_roles.alpha1: half-saturation constant of the lower response
param_roles.alpha2: half-saturation constant of the upper response

FluidTrampoline.blurb: A droplet bouncing on a vibrated soap film that acts as a nonlinear spring — increasing forcing drives simple, multi-periodic, then chaotic bouncing.

param_roles.psi: quadratic-drag energy-loss coefficient of film contact

LotkaVolterra.blurb: Predator and prey circling a neutrally stable centre — a conserved first integral, so every initial condition rides its own closed orbit.

param_roles.alpha: intrinsic growth rate of the prey
param_roles.delta: conversion of consumed prey into predators

CoevolvingPredatorPrey.blurb: An eco-evolutionary predator-prey model where a fast-evolving prey trait feeds back on the populations, generating chaos without external forcing.

param_roles.b1: saturation constant of the functional response
param_roles.b2: saturation constant of the functional response
param_roles.delta: trait-asymmetry parameter of the fitness landscape
param_roles.k1: coupling strength of the fitness landscape
param_roles.k2: coupling strength of the fitness landscape
param_roles.k4: coupling strength of the fitness landscape
param_roles.vv: relative timescale of trait evolution vs population dynamics

Finance.blurb: The Ma-Chen macroeconomic system — interest rate, investment demand, and price index whose quadratic couplings yield a low-dimensional chaotic attractor.

KawczynskiStrizhak.blurb: A three-variable polynomial reduction of the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction reproducing its mixed-mode and period-doubling routes to chaos.

param_roles.beta: constant drive (offset) of the slow recovery variable
param_roles.gamma: timescale / gain of the fast cubic nullcline
param_roles.kappa: relaxation rate of the slowest variable
param_roles.mu: bifurcation parameter shaping the cubic nullcline

FoldedTowel.blurb: Rössler's folded-towel map — the prototypical hyperchaotic map, the lowest dimension admitting two positive Lyapunov exponents.

param_roles.a: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.b: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.c: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.d: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.e: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.f: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences
param_roles.g: map parameter of the coupled quadratic recurrences

GeneralizedHenon.blurb: The Baier-Klein 3-D generalization of the Hénon map — a single quadratic term chained through a delay line, exhibiting hyperchaos.

param_roles.a: nonlinearity strength of the quadratic term
param_roles.b: coupling to the delayed state (volume contraction rate)

Zaslavskii.blurb: The Zaslavsky dissipative standard map — a damped kicked rotor whose contraction folds the standard-map web onto a fractal strange attractor.

param_roles.nu: coupling between action and phase advance
param_roles.r: damping rate (exp(-r) is the per-step action contraction)

Bogdanov.blurb: The discrete-time normal form of the Bogdanov-Takens double-zero bifurcation — invariant circles, Arnold tongues, and chaos near a cusp.

param_roles.k: strength of the quadratic x(x-1) nonlinearity
param_roles.mu: coefficient of the mixed x*y term

Hopalong.blurb: Barry Martin's "Hopalong" map — a square-root-and-sign nonlinearity that sprays iterates into layered ornamental chaotic attractors.

param_roles.a: additive constant in the y-recurrence (overall offset)

Svensson.blurb: A trigonometric planar strange-attractor map whose sines and cosines trace intricate filamentary chaotic attractors.

param_roles.a: angular frequency scaling x inside the trig terms
param_roles.b: angular frequency scaling y inside the trig terms

ZeraouliaSprott.blurb: A minimal 2-D rational map whose x-recurrence is a single non-vanishing fraction — one of the simplest rational maps reaching chaos via a quasi-periodic route.

param_roles.a: gain of the rational x-recurrence (primary control parameter)

Coullet.blurb: The Arneodo–Coullet–Tresser jerk flow in its Volterra regime, whose homoclinic (Shilnikov) connection spawns a spiral strange attractor.

GenesioTesi.blurb: A canonical jerk control system whose single quadratic nonlinearity, analysed by harmonic balance, produces a Shilnikov strange attractor.

ThomasLabyrinth.blurb: Thomas's cyclically symmetric flow at weak damping — a deterministic random walk (labyrinth chaos) across a 3-D lattice of unstable equilibria.

Bouali.blurb: The Bouali business-cycle flow (first regime) — a feedback-augmented Van der Pol oscillator tracing a stretched-loop economic strange attractor.

LiuChen.blurb: A generalized-Lorenz double-scroll flow (Sakarya family) at the Liu–Chen parameters, keeping two quadratic cross-products with no linear cross-coupling.

PanXuZhou.blurb: A two-scroll, Lorenz-like chaotic attractor in the Dequan-Li family at the Pan–Xu–Zhou parameters, where the x·z and x² terms switch off. The catalogue ships k = 28 rather than the paper's k = 16: the published value lies below the Hopf threshold k ≈ 17.27, where the orbit settles onto a stable focus instead of sustaining chaos.

Tsucs2.blurb: The Three-Scroll Unified Chaotic System (TSUCS-2), a Dequan-Li-family flow unifying several three-scroll attractors. At the published parameters the orbit is a bounded, visually three-scroll-like 2-torus rather than a strange attractor: the measured spectrum is (0, 0, −1.50), so treat any "chaotic" quantity from the defaults with suspicion.

CaTwoPlusQuasiperiodic.blurb: The Houart–Dupont–Goldbeter intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillator in its quasiperiodic/chaotic regime, driven by self-modulated InsP₃ feedback.

BelousovZhabotinsky.blurb: The Györgyi–Field three-variable model of deterministic chaos in the oscillating Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction.

BlinkingVortex.blurb: Aref's blinking-vortex flow — the paradigm of chaotic advection, in which two alternately-active agitators stir a passive tracer chaotically.

LidDrivenCavityFlow.blurb: A time-periodic lid-driven cavity whose two-mode wall driving reverses each period, braiding passive tracers into topological chaos.

BickleyJet.blurb: A meandering Bickley (sech²) jet perturbed by three Rossby-wave modes — a benchmark for Lagrangian coherent structures in geophysical flows.

InteriorSquirmer.blurb: The unsteady interior Stokes flow of an oscillating cylindrical squirmer, advecting tracers chaotically through a five-mode surface actuation.

BeerRNN.blurb: A three-neuron continuous-time recurrent neural network (CTRNN) whose fixed weights place it on a chaotic attractor.

Hopfield.blurb: A six-neuron continuous Hopfield network whose recurrent inhibition drives the neural activity chaotic (Lewis–Glass).

MacArthur.blurb: MacArthur's consumer–resource model — five species competing for five substitutable resources by Liebig's law, sustaining chaotic coexistence (the paradox of the plankton).

VossDelay.blurb: Voss's anticipating-synchronization circuit — a scalar delay system with cubic feedback whose broad Lyapunov spectrum marks a high-dimensional delay attractor.
